newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI RUBBER STEADY, TALK OF GOVT STOCK SALE SWIRLS.
newsitem.headline: THAI RUBBER STEADY, TALK OF GOVT STOCK SALE SWIRLS.

text.p: Thai rubber prices were steady to lower this week, pressured by rumours that the government planned to unwind its stock, trade sources said on Friday.
Despite repeated denials from the authorities, some market players were still cautious and remained sidelined, they said.
Sanit Samosorn, deputy director general of the agriculture department, reiterated on Friday that the government had no plans to sell its stock now.
But he confirmed that the government had more than 70,000 tonnes of rubber in stock.
"There is no plan to sell now. The price would be pressured further if we do that. What would be the point of intervention then?" he said.

Rumours have swirled in the market that the government's effort to balance the budget in order to meet the preconditions from the International Monetary Fund for a financial package could force it to sell the rubber and drop the intervention scheme.
Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said he planned to shed 600 billion baht from the budget for fiscal 1998, starting October, to keep it balanced.
Trade was thin as real consumer demand was lacking and the bearish tone was expected to continue next week.
Benchmark RSS3 was indicated around 97.00-98.00 U.S. cents per kg FOB Bangkok for October shipment and 100 U.S. cents on the same basis for December shipment.
